subject: Chemistry
title: Mercury: The Cure That Killed
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Mercury: The Cure That Killed.

hook.text: For centuries, doctors prescribed mercury to treat syphilis, depression, and constipation. It poisoned more than it cured.

buildup.text: Mercury compounds were rubbed on skin, inhaled as vapor, or swallowed as calomel (mercury chloride) pills.

discovery.text: Mercury did kill syphilis bacteria—but it also destroyed kidneys, gums, and the nervous system. Patients lost teeth and sanity.

twist.text: Abraham Lincoln took mercury pills for depression. Historians believe the mercury worsened his famous mood swings.

climax.text: Mercury was used in medicine until the 1900s. Its removal from most products only completed in the 2000s.

punchline.text: A cure worse than the disease. Mercury killed bacteria and patients alike.

quiz.question: Why was mercury used as medicine for so long despite being toxic?
options: It actually did kill disease-causing bacteria, so patients sometimes improved
Doctors didn't know mercury was a chemical element
Mercury was the only substance available in apothecaries

details.summary: Mercury compounds were widely used as medicines from ancient times through the early 20th century to treat syphilis, intestinal parasites, and various other conditions..
details.whyItMatters: Mercury medicine represents a cautionary tale in pharmaceutical history. Its prolonged use despite evident toxicity helped establish the need for evidence-based medicine and drug safety testing.
takeaways: Calomel was prescribed for nearly every ailment in 18th and 19th century medicine
Mercury poisoning from treatment caused kidney failure and neurological damage
The mercury era helped motivate modern drug safety and efficacy requirements

faq.question: Why did doctors continue prescribing mercury when it clearly harmed patients?
faq.answer: Mercury treatment produced visible effects like excessive salivation and diarrhea that doctors interpreted as the body purging disease. The prevailing humoral theory valued purging as therapeutic. Without controlled studies, doctors could not distinguish drug effects from disease course.

faq.question: Which historical figures were likely harmed by mercury treatments?
faq.answer: Abraham Lincoln reportedly took mercury-containing blue mass pills for depression. Many syphilis patients received mercury rubs and ingestion for decades. Several European monarchs received mercury treatments. Hair analysis of historical figures frequently reveals elevated mercury levels.
